title: TerminalX for Windows
description: The Rift Works console for network engineers: serial, telnet and SSH in one window, with an AI Helper reading the console beside you, an IP scanner and a TFTP server as tabs.

details.label: Installs to
details.value: Your own user profile (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\TerminalX); no administrator password needed

details.label: Needs
details.value: An internet connection during the install: Claude Code and Memora are set up for the Helper when they are not on the PC yet

details.label: Account needed
details.value: A Claude account for the Helper, signed in from the app. Consoles, the scanner and TFTP work without one

details.label: Updates
details.value: TerminalX checks here every 10 minutes and offers a new version; nothing is installed until you say so

whats_new.heading: What's new in 0.2.0
items: Updates from GitHub. TerminalX looks at the project's GitHub Releases every 10 minutes and when it starts; a new version shows in the status bar and under gear â†’ Check for updates, with its notes. Download, then Install and restart: the setup runs over the installed copy and TerminalX comes back on the new version. Each download is checked against the SHAâ€‘256 published with the release. Settings â†’ Updates holds the switch, the repository and an access token for a private repository.

The setup knows what is there. Welcome says which version is on the PC already and that an install updates it, and if GitHub has a newer setup than the one running, offers to fetch and run that instead.
New name. CodeKnife is now TerminalX. The program, the setup, the Start Menu entry and the Apps & features entry all carry the new name.

Nothing lost. On the first start under the new name, settings, saved hosts, session logs and the TFTP folder are copied from the old %APPDATA%\CodeKnife folder when the new one does not exist yet. The old folder is left in place.
Environment variables are now TERMINALX_* (TERMINALX_HOSTS_FILE, TERMINALX_CLAUDE, TERMINALX_NO_LOGIN, TERMINALX_PTY_DEBUG).

install.heading: How to install
steps: Click Download, then open TerminalXSetup.exe when it finishes.
If Windows SmartScreen warns about an unrecognised app, choose More info, then Run anyway. The setup is not code-signed yet.
Accept the license agreement, choose the folder and shortcuts, and click Install. If TerminalX is already on this PC this updates it and keeps your settings, hosts and logs.

verify.heading: Verify your download (optional)
verify.note: The file checksum changes with every release. In PowerShell: Get-FileHash TerminalXSetup.exe -Algorithm SHA256.
